key_insight: Extending tabulated chemistry with preferential and differential diffusion in RANS lets the model capture the key thermo-diffusive behavior of lean hydrogen flames much more faithfully than unity-Lewis treatments.
engineering_relevance: This improves the predictive reliability of low-cost CFD for hydrogen combustors and burner design, especially where flame length, heat release, and stability depend on diffusion effects.
method: Solved transport equations for progress variable and mixture fraction from species equations with mixture-averaged diffusion and Soret effect.
Added turbulence–chemistry interaction through a presumed PDF closure within a RANS framework.
Compared against DNS and against unity-Lewis and thermo-diffusion-only variants to isolate model effects.
evidence_signal: Against DNS at Re = 5500 and 11000, the model reproduced flame length, heat-release distribution, and the equivalence-ratio/super-adiabatic temperature branches of the slot flame.
watch_item: Performance still depends on turbulence closures for scalar dissipation, turbulent diffusion, and Reynolds stresses, which may limit robustness across different flame configurations.
paper_title: Preferential and differential diffusion in RANS simulation of lean hydrogen flames with tabulated chemistry
